properties.description: Small Hellenistic odeion (c. 2nd century BC), part of the gymnasium complex; largely reconstructed in the 20th century based on limited remains.
properties.name: Ωδείο
properties.note: Structure is heavily reconstructed (mostly modern restoration); only limited original remains survive. Music events are held at the venue.

properties.description: Hellenistic stadium (rebuilt after 227/226 BC earthquake), 200.76 m (600 Rhodian feet) long. Site of the Halieia festival dedicated to Helios. Capacity 28,000-30,000 spectators.
properties.name: Αρχαίο Στάδιο

notes: Three principal contiguous surviving monuments in the Rhodes Acropolis archaeological park: whole native Apollo temple platform with three standing Doric shafts/L-shaped entablature/fourth broken shaft and low foundation remains; complete restored rectangular east-facing Odeon with open orchestra, lower10/upper9 stone seat tiers, radial stairs, walkway, retaining walls/side ramps; and whole long stadium surviving low stone seating banks/curved south end/open north end. No lost temple roof/cella/peristyle, intact Classical reconstruction, other park sanctuaries/gymnasium/library/underground shrines, precinct ground/bedrock/trees/stadium-earth slab, visitors/scaffolds/signs or city. This bounded three-monument ensemble is not every archaeological feature in the wider Acropolis.
